question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the positive $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $k\sqrt[3]{x}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant. If $P$ has velocity $v=2\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has velocity $v=8\,m/s$ when its displacement is $8\,m,$ find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14164351/assets/771929267e75b5d45b9777399c784fafc570386834eee6738fead9ff1bb78e5e.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $k\sqrt[3]{x}\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=k\sqrt[3]{x}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=k\sqrt[3]{x}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int k\sqrt[3]{x}\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(2)^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}(0)^{4/3}+C \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+2.
$$

Finally, since $v=8\,m/s$ when $x=8\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+2 \\ \frac{1}{2}(8)^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}(8)^{4/3}+2 \\ 32 & =12k+2 \\ 12k & =30 \\ k & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
